title: Joining the Sig Meyers band
summary: Pay, hours, ten-man lineup and personnel; four years five months with Sig Meyers.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Uh, I also slipped up on a good one. What's that?

Oh, you tell me about it. You asked me some time ago about what happened when I left the Playhouse. Well, I worked the Playhouse. Well, I worked the Playhouse. And it was through the New Orleans Rhythm King at Friars Inn that I went to work with Sig Meyers. Uh, when Sig approached me about the thing, he didn't offer me much money, but he offered me a short job. And that was, uh, 8.30 till 12. It was five sessions a week. Uh, Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday night, Sunday night, and Sunday afternoon. Three hours on Sunday afternoon. So I kept dickering back and forth with Sig Meyers about the job. I told him I didn't need the job. He needed me worse than I needed the job. So we finally got, we finally got together and we finally, I finally settled for $95 a week. And I was there a couple of months with him and he gave me $5 raise because I knew that other fellas were getting $100. And I knew Don Gooden well that what I added to the band was worth the other five and Sig knew it. So I just added it.
Was that a big band, huh?
Oh, yes. It was ten men.
That was the day when the swing was starting to come in.

Oh, yeah. Uh-huh. Ten men. They had, oh, Sig had some good men in his band. He had fellas like Bollie DeFoe, Muxi Spania, uh, uh, Bob Buscelli. I haven't heard much of him recently. He, wait, in the last 20 years or so, I think Bob had just wrapped up. He went in for the motion picture business. He didn't care too much about the, uh, music. Shorty Williamson, Georgie Petroni, Earl Andrews. Sig played fiddle. Sig played fiddle, yes. I was with the band, too. Did he double on anything else? No. A good part of the time he just waved his bow. Uh-huh. But Sig was a good school musician. Uh-huh. I think that he could have... Well, you were with him a long time, aren't you? I was with him, uh, 53 months. Good night. Uh, have you ever heard a fellow named Marvin Saxby? Yeah. Well, Saxby was the guitar player. Uh, Saxby was an exceptional, outstanding guy at that time. As a matter of fact, uh, when, uh, the first amplifiers came out, uh, Lyon and Healey hired Sykesby to demonstrate him in the afternoon. And I understand the pay was pretty good. Of course, I don't know what he got, but he said he was getting well paid. So I stayed with Sig four years and five months. And then my good friend Muggsy, he was causing me to leave in Sig. Because, uh, you see, I was the highest priced man in the band. After all those years. I was getting real money. And Sig paid in check. I made the mistake one night of cashing my check at the drugstore on the corner. And, uh, devil-faced Muggsy Spania saw it. And that started the trouble. Uh, Sig didn't want me to quit, but I told him I didn't want to work with people like that. And I knew he wouldn't fire Muggsy. So, all right. Rap work with Sig, too, you know. Rap over. Oh, yeah. And the same band with you? No, I didn't. You know, no, it was just before I joined him. Uh, Sig had about the fastest band in Chicago at that time.
